Game Jams are great. They're intended to draw attention to skill, talent, creativity, and a solid grounding in the basics of game design. That doesn't mean the games that come out of them are market-worthy, no matter how they're promoted.

That includes the free marketing they get when their own promotional offerings are linked to on news aggregate sites. If the premise of the game bothers you so much, why draw attention to it? It just increases its chances of being greenlit.

Journey for example (PS3 and I think maybe PS4 port) was a neat little game that lasted a couple hours where your character was just a faceless silhouette with clothing robes over them. The only way to communicate with someone you had connected online with was a quick little chirp sound. Talk about minimalistic. And it probably got a few awards for it's art direction, which was also very neat. At the end of it, it showed the PSN ID of each player you had connected to and joined you/them at some point. Very neat idea, and I'd like to see more sorta 'risky'' ideas like this being done.
